purpose: Fluphenazine decanoate is used to treat schizophrenia and other conditions that cause symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and confused thinking. It is a long-acting injectable form of the medication, meaning you only need a shot every 2 to 4 weeks instead of taking a daily pill. This makes it easier to stay on your treatment and helps keep your symptoms under control.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking certain chemical messengers in your brain called dopamine receptors. When there is too much dopamine activity in certain parts of the brain, it can cause symptoms like hearing voices or seeing things that are not there. By calming down that overactivity, fluphenazine helps reduce those distressing symptoms and helps you think more clearly.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include muscle stiffness, restlessness, or shakiness (similar to Parkinson's-like movements). You may also feel drowsy, dizzy, or have a dry mouth. Some people notice blurred vision, constipation, or weight changes. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious movement disorder called tardive dyskinesia, which may be permanent, so tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual face or body movements. It can also cause a rare but dangerous condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, with symptoms like high fever, muscle rigidity, and confusion — seek emergency help if this happens. This medication is not recommended for elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis, as it can increase the risk of stroke or death. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin or into a muscle, usually every 2 to 4 weeks. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you, typically starting low (around 12.5 mg) and adjusting as needed. Because it is long-acting, your doctor will monitor you closely to make sure the dose is working well for you.
